page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the left margin. The left margin holds one note, set beside the lines "nobili ad hoc" to "misso". Below the text there is nothing but a catchword at the right.
page.running_head: De Agro Frif. inter Lavic. & Amaf.

main_text.p: Maximiliani filio, gubernatio tota & omne in Frisiam jus ad eundem transiret. Albertus per suos, quos præmiserat, oppressis omnibus Translavicanis, atque à fœdere Groningano vi & aperto bello aversis, inque fidem suam adactis, Groningam quoque & agrum vicinum tentavit. Nam hos quoque ad imperium sibi commissum pertinere ferebat, habebatque pro se interpretem controversiæ Maximilianum. Verùm cùm res per intercessiones & colloquia non procederet, ipse ob filii casum, quem Translavicani Franekeræ obsederant, secundò in Frisiam veniens, liberato filio, & rebus Translavicanis pro tempore constitutis, exercitum cis Lavicam adduxit, nullo-que negotio agrum in suam potestatem & fidem redegit. Sed in obsidenda urbe dum hæret, intercedente rursum Georgio Thorenio Equestris dignitatis viro Albertus Groningā obsdet.nobili ad hoc à Principibus Germaniæ misso, & cum eo Friderico Badensi episcopo Ultrajectino, colloquium denuò coiit, anno M. page.notes: The marginal note reads "Albertus / Groningā / obsdet." Its last word is hard to read at this scan resolution; the letter after "obs" may be an i, so the reading "obsdet." is doubtful. The last line of the page is "bel-", continued by "lum" at the right, which I have given as the catchword. Greek and Hebrew do not occur on this page. The gray credit line at the bottom right of the scan is the digitiser's mark and is not transcribed.
